_doc: Real TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi through rosbridge (src/robot/real_robot.py, UTS-RI/turtlebot_rosbridge). Check every value on the lab robot with python experiments/check_robot.py HOST before a mission.
_host: IP of the robot's rosbridge server, 192.168.1.2XX where XX is the TurtleBot ID (lab wifi turtlebot-MMR); main.py --real HOST and check_robot.py HOST override it
_topics: rosbridge_api defaults; replace with the names from ros2 topic list on the robot if they differ
_wheel_joints: names in /joint_states, picked by name; seen on the lab robot on 23 Oct (results/hardware/20261023_*/report.json)
_wheel_sign: +1 when the joint position grows as the robot rolls forward; confirmed on 23 Oct: check_robot.py --drive gave +0.10 m on both wheels for a forward command (results/hardware/20261023_122823)
_v_max: m/s and rad/s, first-run safety caps on top of the Waffle Pi limits (0.26, 1.82). Commands above a cap are scaled down together, so the turning radius v/w is kept. Raise them once the lab speed rule is known and the robot behaves
_min_coverage: fraction of the forward (+-90 deg) LiDAR beams that must return before the robot moves (config/control.json lidar_obs, 0.8 in the sim). The lab panels are black foam, which the LDS-01 does not see: on 28 Oct the forward coverage was 0.55 at the stage-1 start and 0.34-0.38 at the stage-2 start (nothing from -10 to +70 deg although the left panel was 1.5 m ahead), so the mission waited at 0.8 and at 0.4. 0.2 still stops the robot when the LiDAR is blocked or broken. The LiDAR sees the white marker stands and the orange box, not the panels: the panels are kept off by the waypoints, not the LiDAR
_max_sensor_age: s; step() stops the robot and raises if /joint_states or /scan is older than this (lost wifi, crashed driver)
_connect_timeout: s to wait for the rosbridge connection and then for the first message on each sensor topic
